items.title: The AI Marketing Paradox: More Content, Harder Decisions - BW Marketing World
items.raw_summary: Generative AI has solved the problem of producing creative work. It has created a harder one: deciding what deserves to reach a consumer.Marketers are no longer debating whether to use AI. India is setting the pace. BCG’s 2026 global survey of CMOs found 57 per cent of Indian CMOs fund AI directly from marketing budgets, against 47 per cent globally. About 53 per cent of Indian CMOs expect 5-9 per cent incremental topline growth from AI, against a global average of 43 per cent, the highest of any region.Volume Is Not The ProblemShruti Kaushik, Group Chief Marketing Officer at DivyaSree Developers, filters on three criteria. She says, “There are three things I look at while shortlisting the thousand ads: brand distinctiveness, consumer preference and business objectives. Brand values and brand ethos non-negotiable. Finally, while AI can generate multiple ads and help us shortlist them, it is our judgement that determines the strategy. Human intervention is always needed to provide the right strategic input.”Chandan Mukherji, CEO of Engrowi, puts strategy first and data second. He states, “Today, Gen AI can create dozens and hundreds of pieces of content in a very short period of time. The first and foremost thing is to think about the brand, the strategy and the objective they want to achieve through those pieces of content.”After that comes optimisation. “There are today a number of AI tools that can also help you pre-decide what kind of content to go in for, using predictive intelligence tools. There are, of course, ways and means through which you can put it out in the real world and also see what kind of traction each piece of content is getting. You can then narrow down the different options,” he adds.Further Mukherji explains, “Brand and brand strategy are the most important areas where judgement comes into play. But there are also technologies like AI and real-world metrics that can help you take the right decision.”What Is Working, And What Is NotAbhijit Bhattacharya, CMO and Senior Vice President at DLF, says the pilot phase is over and a few use cases are paying off. “Three or four use cases are working across organisations. The first is content creation using Generative AI. The ability to create content at scale and for different use cases and contexts is very important. I think this is working across organisations,” he says.“The second, which is very important to us, is lead management, where you’re able to look at leads, score them and prioritise them. That’s another area that’s working. The third is media buying and measuring advertising effectiveness,” he adds.Bhattacharya also sees agents taking on routine work. “A lot of conversation management is also moving towards Agentic AI. Mundane tasks are increasingly being handed over to AI agents. These are the three or four large areas where I see AI making a difference.”In India, an EY study found that 84-88 per cent of adopters report medium to high business impact, yet most brands still rely on standalone tools rather than integrated systems. Agentic AI is further behind. A Modern Retail survey found 54 per cent of respondents’ companies do not use it in their workflows.The Funnel Without The WebsiteThe bigger shift may be in how consumers find brands at all. Search engine optimisation (SEO) aimed to bring people to a brand’s site. Answer engine optimisation (AEO) and generative engine optimisation (GEO) aim to get a brand named inside an AI-generated answer. In the BCG survey, 90 per. cent of CMOs agreed that generative AI is already reshaping how consumers discover and evaluate brands.Bhattacharya says this is a different game from SEO. He comments, “It’s fundamentally different because SEO was a technology, so to say, that got people onto your website, and you controlled the narrative to a large extent.”“Today, people don’t even come to your website. They form an opinion about your brand, and you are either in the purchase funnel or outside it without them visiting any of your assets. So, it’s important to maintain consistency and have the right information across assets that you do not own, to control that narrative. This ensures that people not only have a favourable opinion of your brand but also choose your brand for the right reasons. So, that’s very important,” he adds.Salesforce’s India findings show 81 per cent of Indian marketers have adopted AI, and that high-performing marketers are 2.2 times more likely than underperformers to have optimised for AI search.
